{{Short description|Greek physicist (born 1955)}}
'''Ignatios Antoniadis''' (born 2 December 1955 in [[Chios]]),<ref>Biographical information from brief biography in ''International Symposium Subnuclear Physics'', [[Pontifical Academy of Sciences]], 2011</ref> is a Greek theoretical physicist, specializing in [[string theory]] and [[particle physics]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.hellenicaworld.com/Greece/Person/en/IAntoniadis.html |title=Ignatios Antoniadis |website=Hellenica World }}</ref>

==Education and career==
Antoniadis received in 1977 a degree in mathematics from the [[University of Athens]] and in 1978 a ''[[Diplôme d'études approfondies]]'' (DEA) in theoretical physics from [[Pierre and Marie Curie University]]. He received in 1980 his ''Thèse de troisème cycle'' (doctorate; thesis title: "''Factorisation des singularités de masse et ses applications''"<ref>{{Cite book |last=Antoniadis |first=Ignace |url=https://www.sudoc.fr/042353041 |title=Factorisation des singularités de masse et ses applications |date=1980 |publisher=Université de Paris-Sud. Faculté des sciences d'Orsay (Essonne) |year=1980}}</ref>) from the [[École normale supérieure]] and in 1983 his ''Thèse d'État'' [higher doctorate; thesis title: ''Au delà du modèle standard U(1) × SU(2) × SU(3)''<ref>{{Cite book |last=Antoniadis |first=Ignatios |url=https://www.sudoc.fr/192733664 |title=Au delà du modèle standard U(1) × SU(2) × SU(3) |date=1983 |publisher=Université de Paris-Sud. Faculté des sciences d'Orsay (Essonne) |year=1983}}</ref>]  from the [[École polytechnique]]. (In 1984 the French academic system replaced the ''Thése d'État'' with the [[habilitation]].) At [[French National Centre for Scientific Research|''Centre national de la recherche scientifique'']] (CNRS), he was from 1982 to 1986 an ''[[Academic ranks in France|attaché de recherche]]'' at the ''Centre de physique théorique'' (CPHT) of the École polytechnique; during those years he was also from 1983 to 1986 a research associate at [[SLAC]]. At [[CNRS]], he was from 1986 to 1992 a ''[[Academic ranks in France|chargé de recherche]]'' and from 1992 to 2015 a ''[[Academic ranks in France|directeur de recherche, class 2]]'' and is from 2015 to the present a ''directeur of recherche, class 1''. At [[CERN]] in Geneva, Switzerland, he was from 1986 to 1988 a fellow, from 1996 to 1997 a scientific associate, and from 2000 to 2014 a senior staff member. From 1997 to 2009 he was a part-time [[Academic ranks in France|''professeur chargé des cours'']] at the École polytechnique.<ref name=mdpi>{{cite web|url=https://www.mdpi.com/about/announcements/3068 |title=Prof. Dr. Ignatios Antoniadis Appointed Editor-in-Chief of Astronomy |website=MDPI (Multidisciplinary Digital Publishing Institute) }}</ref> In 2011 he gave a talk ''Testing strings at the LHC?'' at the international symposium on subnuclear physics held in Vatican City.<ref>{{cite book|editor=Sánchez Sorondo, Marcelo|editor-link=Marcelo Sánchez Sorondo|editor2=Zichichi, Antonino|editor-link2=Antonino Zichichi|chapter=''Testing strings at the LHC?'' by Ignatios Antoniadis|pages=497–502|title=Subnuclear Physics: Past, Present and Future; Proceedings of the International Symposium, held 30 October - 2 November 2011, held in Vatican City|series=Scripta Varia, volume 119|publisher=[[Pontifical Academy of Sciences]]|year=2014|chapter-url=https://www.pas.va/content/dam/casinapioiv/pas/pdf-volumi/scripta-varia/sv119/sv119-antoniadis.pdf}}</ref> At the Albert Einstein Center of the [[University of Bern]],<ref>{{cite web|title=Albert Einstein Center|website=University of Bern|date=3 July 2023 |url=https://www.einstein.unibe.ch/index_eng.html}}</ref> he was a senior scientist from 2014 to 2020.<ref name=mdpi/> In 2021, for six months, he held the [[Francqui Foundation#Francqui Chairs|International Francqui Professorship in Exact Sciences]]<ref>{{cite web|title=International Francqui Professor|url=http://www.francquifoundation.be/new-page/international-francqui-professor/}}</ref> at [[KU Leuven]]-[[Université Libre de Bruxelles]] (ULB)-[[Vrije Universiteit Brussel]] (VUB).<ref name=mdpi/> He was at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] from February 2023 to May 2023 and from September 2024 to July 2025.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ias.edu/scholars/ignatios-antoniadis |title=Ignatios Antoniadis - Scholars &#124; Institute for Advanced Study |website=www.ias.edu |date=4 January 2022 }}</ref>

Antoniadis deals with string theory, tests of string theoretical dualities, [[quantum gravity]], [[supersymmetry]], and [[Grand Unified Theory|grand unified theories]] (GUTs). He played an important role in the development of superstring theory models in four dimensions (fermionic construction).<ref>{{cite arXiv |author=Antoniadis, Ignatios|title=Review of free-fermionic 4d string models |year=1993|eprint=hep-th/9307002 }}</ref> He is particularly known for his investigations into the possible phenomenology of [[superstring theory]] (''e.g.'', grand unified theories at low energies; statements about the particle spectrum; possibly observable effects such as extra dimensions;<ref name=Gravitymod>{{cite journal|doi=10.1088/1742-6596/68/1/012013 |title=Gravity modifications from extra dimensions |year=2007 |last1=Antoniadis |first1=I. |journal=Journal of Physics: Conference Series |volume=68 |issue=1 |article-number=012013 |bibcode=2007JPhCS..68a2013A |s2cid=250669271 |doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|doi=10.1002/prop.201100072 |title=Physics of extra dimensions |year=2011 |last1=Antoniadis |first1=I. |journal=Fortschritte der Physik |volume=59 |issue=11–12 |pages=1127–1134 |bibcode=2011ForPh..59.1127A |arxiv=hep-ph/0512182 }}</ref> and possible change in gravitational force at short distances).<ref>{{cite journal|doi=10.1088/1742-6596/33/1/015|url=https://iopscience.iop.org/article/10.1088/1742-6596/33/1/015/meta |title=Physics of extra dimensions |year=2006 |last1=Antoniadis |first1=I. |journal=Journal of Physics: Conference Series |volume=33 |issue=1 |pages=170–181 |bibcode=2006JPhCS..33..170A |s2cid=250673789 |arxiv=hep-ph/0512182 }}</ref><ref name=Gravitymod />

Antoniadis was awarded in 1995 the Greek Bodossaki Foundation Prize, in 2000 the silver medal of the CNRS, and in 2002 the Special Prize of the ''[[Société Française de Physique]]'' (SFP). In 1995 the [[University of Ioannina]] gave him an honorary doctorate. In 2008 he received an Advanced Grant from the European Research Commission (ERC).<ref name=mdpi/>
